Test exposure-by-celltype interaction

Source: R/interaction.R
run_interaction_test.Rd

Formally tests whether an exposure effect differs across cell types using a pseudobulk interaction model. This prevents the common mistake of concluding "the exposure affects cell type A but not B" based on separate per- celltype p-values (Gelman & Stern 2006).

Usage

run_interaction_test(
  x,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  target_genes = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L,
  min_donors = 5L
)

Arguments

x

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

exposure

Character. Exposure variable name.

celltype_col

Character. colData column with cell type labels. Default "cell_type".

target_genes

Character vector (optional). Genes to test. Default: top 50 most variable genes across all cell types.

covariates

Character vector (optional). Columns of exposureData adjusted for; listing the exposure here is an error.

min_cells

Integer. Min cells per donor per celltype. Default 10.

min_donors

Integer. Min donors per celltype. Default 5.

Value

A DataFrame with columns: gene, p_interaction (F-test for the exposure-by-cell-type terms), df_interaction (numerator degrees of freedom), padj_interaction (BH-corrected), n_celltypes, n_donors.

Details

For each gene, pseudobulk log-CPM values of all cell types are stacked, one row per donor and cell type, and two linear models are compared with an F-test:


reduced: y ~ donor + celltype + covariates:celltype
full:    y ~ donor + celltype + covariates:celltype + exposure:celltype

Donor fixed effects absorb every donor-level quantity, including the exposure and covariate main effects, and the shared donor component of expression in different cell types, so the test compares exposure slopes between cell types through within-donor contrasts rather than treating cell types from the same donor as independent. Covariate-by-cell-type terms allow covariate effects to differ between cell types. Donors observed in only one cell type do not inform the interaction.

Comparing significance levels across cell types is not the same as testing for a difference between them (Gelman & Stern 2006, Nieuwenhuis et al. 2011); this function tests the difference directly.

References

Gelman A, Stern H (2006). The difference between 'significant' and 'not significant' is not itself statistically significant. Am Stat 60:328-331.

Nieuwenhuis S et al. (2011). Erroneous analyses of interactions in neuroscience. Nat Neurosci 14:1105-1107. doi:10.1038/nn.2886

Examples

library(SingleCellExperiment); library(S4Vectors)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(5000, 8), nrow = 50,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:50), paste0("c", 1:100)))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = DataFrame(cell_id = paste0("c", 1:100),
        donor_id = rep(paste0("D", 1:10), each = 10),
        cell_type = rep(c("Mono", "NK"), 50)))
exp_mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), nrow = 10,
    dimnames = list(paste0("D", 1:10), c("E1", "E2")))
scee <- build_scee(sce, exp_mat, sample_col = "donor_id")
ix <- run_interaction_test(scee, exposure = "E1",
    celltype_col = "cell_type", min_cells = 3L, min_donors = 3L)
head(ix)
